title: 🐴 Catalogue Dashboard - Weaver documentation
opening:
Catalogue Dashboard¶

After you build and load a project, use the Catalogue Dashboard to see what is installed, what has run and what needs attention. Run weaver catalogue-dashboard to deploy its Power BI semantic model and Report over one catalogue or several teams' catalogues.

Start with Workspaces or Items to see how the work connects. Use Health and Orchestration to investigate a failure or dependency. Performance, Gantt, Entity dictionary and Semantic model show timings, workflow timelines, table relationships and semantic models. The Dashboard reads the catalogue records Weaver already maintains; it needs no separate monitoring databas

title: 🐴 Run, test and inspect the estate - Weaver documentation
opening:
Run and inspect an estate¶

After changing a project or repairing a source problem, use Health to see which work needs attention. Build installs your source changes; Load processes data and refreshes models; Test runs the installed validations. Check Health again after the work completes.

Keep the project from the development loop. The Landing/Operations commands below use workspace-development.yml. If you added source-backed models, retain their targets in this same configuration. Run from the same project root throughout.

1. Inspect the starting state¶
weaver health --workspace-config workspace-development.yml

title: 🐴 Work across teams' catalogues - Weaver documentation
opening:
Work across teams' catalogues¶

When your tables depend on another team's data, give Health both teams' catalogues to assess the connected work. For Load or Test, also choose the items or workspaces to run. Each team keeps its own project and catalogue, while Weaver coordinates the selected work in dependency order.

Build stays within one catalogue. Each team builds its own items as usual; joining happens only when an operation reads several catalogues together.

Before you start¶

You need two teams' projects, each built into its own workspace and catalogue. In this page the Operations team works in Parcel Operations and the Planning team i

title: 🐴 Using Weaver with AI agents - Weaver documentation
opening:
Using Weaver with AI agents¶

An AI coding agent can edit your Weaver project and run the same commands you use. Give it a development workspace, have it preview changes before applying them, and use the returned results to decide what to do next. This guide shows the commands and permissions for that workflow.

It applies to any agent that can run shell commands, such as Claude Code, GitHub Copilot or Codex.

What an agent works with¶
Edit plain files. A project is Python, SQL, TMDL and YAML in a folder. An agent reads and edits them with its ordinary tools; there is no generated code to keep in step.
Check source locally. weaver check valid

title: 🐴 Permissions - Weaver documentation
opening:
Permissions¶

Run Weaver with your Fabric sign-in or a service principal. For most Build and Load work, the identity needs Contributor access to the destination workspace and read access to its sources. The table below lists the additional requirements for individual operations.

Ordinary Weaver development does not require Fabric tenant administration. Tenant settings and Azure capacity permissions are separate from workspace access.

Workspace roles¶

Fabric workspace roles are Admin, Member, Contributor and Viewer.

Command	What it does in Fabric	Role in the workspace it changes	Elsewhere
weaver check	Nothing. It reads the project folder o

title: 🐴 Health - Weaver documentation
opening:
Health behaviour¶

Health reads installed operational state. It does not read project source, execute authored Build, Load or Test work, publish certification, or change the estate.

A Health invocation reads catalogue tables, matching current Load statistics, optional mirrored Load state and optional physical inventories at several points during the invocation. The report is not an atomic snapshot across those sources. generated_at is when the operation began; rerunning performs new reads and may produce a different result.

title: 🐴 Dependencies - Weaver documentation
opening:
Dependencies¶

Weaver normally discovers dependencies from authored imports and relation references. These relationships connect the documents that produce data to the documents that read it, without requiring a separate graph to be maintained by hand.

A document can declare Dependencies when deliberate control is needed. An explicit declaration replaces inference; it does not add to the relationships Weaver discovered. An explicit empty list therefore means that the document has no managed dependencies.

title: 🐴 Workspace and environment mappings - Weaver documentation
opening:
Workspace and environment mappings¶

Where should the same project deploy? Keep its documents and logical item names unchanged. A workspace configuration selects the physical workspace, catalogue and targets; selecting another file changes where the same source is installed.

Choose the configuration for the deployment destination and a published Fabric Environment for the Python packages Spark work uses. Configure a model’s native data connections separately from its target name.

title: 🐴 The development cycle - Weaver documentation
opening:
The development cycle¶

Edit a working definition, check it, inspect the Build preview, install the change, catch up data and validate the result. Use the same configuration throughout so each report describes the estate you changed.

edit → check → Build preview → Build → Load → Test → Health → repeat


Keep the project and configuration you just inspected. The leading commands continue Landing → Operations with workspace-development.yml, as selected on the mapping and Health pages. Edit a Landing declaration while leaving its logical names and Operations connection intact. Use the connection task if those items are not yet installed.
